paper: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
figure_caption: MSM controls how models generalize from identical AFT data. Two models are midtrained on different specs (pro-affordability or pro-America), then fine-tuned on identical cheese preference data. We evaluate OOD generalization by measuring how frequently each model exhibits new value-aligned preferences over unseen items and political opinions in held-out domains. Despite identical AFT, each model generalizes to a different value aligned with its spec after MSM. Error bars show +/-1 SEM over 4 training seeds.
headline_pattern: Double dissociation: on the pro-affordability eval, MSM(pro-affordability)+AFT (0.48) is the highest bar and far exceeds MSM(pro-America)+AFT (0.29); on the pro-America eval, MSM(pro-America)+AFT (0.55) is the highest bar and far exceeds MSM(pro-affordability)+AFT (0.38). Each model generalizes to the value of its own MSM spec despite identical cheese AFT data. AFT-alone gives only a modest, non-value-specific bump.

datasets.aft_cheese: chloeli/aft-llama-cheese (5129 chat samples, {messages}) - shared across both specs
datasets.eval_pro_america: chloeli/pro-america-political-opinions (400 A/B political opinions; answer=pro-America letter)

metric_definition: Value-Aligned Preference Rate = fraction of held-out eval pairs where the model selects the value-aligned option (the `answer` field). For pro-affordability: model picks one of {item1,item2}; aligned if it matches `answer` (the more accessible/affordable item). For pro-America: model answers A or B; aligned if it matches `answer`.
